content:
1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |
55: |----------|:----:|----------|
56: | Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
57: | Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
58: | Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
59: | Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
60: | Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
61: | Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
62: | Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
63: | Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
64: | Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
65: | Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
66: | Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
67: | Risk Profiling | 1 | suitability score → suggested equity/debt split |
68: | Advisor | 1 | `create_financial_plan` — the story → plan orchestrator |
69: 
70: Browse them all (with live descriptions) at [`/tools`](https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/tools).
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## Quick start
75: 
76: ### Use the hosted connector (no install)
77: 
78: **Claude Desktop** — Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste:
79: 
80: ```
81: https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
82: ```
83: 
84: **Claude Code**
85: 
86: ```bash
87: claude mcp add --transport http personal-finance https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
88: ```
89: 
90: **Cursor / VS Code** — add to `mcp.json`:
91: 
92: ```json
93: {
94:   "mcpServers": {
95:     "personal-finance": {
96:       "url": "https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp",
97:       "transport": "http"
98:     }
99:   }
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: ### Install from PyPI (stdio server)
104: 
105: ```bash
106: pip install personal-finance-mcp     # or: uvx personal-finance-mcp
107: ```
108: 
109: Then point Claude Desktop at it:
110: 
111: ```json
112: {
113:   "mcpServers": {
114:     "personal-finance": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["personal-finance-mcp"] }
115:   }
116: }
117: ```
118: 
119: ### Run locally from source
120: 
121: ```bash
122: git clone https://github.com/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp.git
123: cd personal-finance-mcp
124: pip install -e .
125: 
126: # Option A — classic stdio MCP server (offline, no web)
127: python -m src
128: 
129: # Option B — unified server: website + /mcp connector + /api  (http://localhost:7860)
130: cd web && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
131: python -m src.web
132: ```
133: 
134: For stdio, point Claude Desktop at the local process:
135: 
136: ```json
137: {
138:   "mcpServers": {
139:     "personal-finance": { "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "src"] }
140:   }
141: }
142: ```
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: ## The website
147:

content:
1: """
2: Personal Finance MCP Server
3: 
4: A stateless MCP server providing deterministic personal finance calculations
5: for financial planning, investment analysis, and portfolio management.
6: 
7: Supports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and any MCP-compatible client.
8: Transport: stdio (default), SSE (optional).
9: """
10: 
11: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
12: from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings
13: from .tools import (
14:     tvm,
15:     debt,
16:     planning,
17:     bonds,
18:     stocks,
19:     mutual_funds,
20:     portfolio,
21:     derivatives,
22:     india_savings,
23:     cashflow,
24:     risk_profile,
25:     advisor,
26:     marketdata,
27: )
28: 
29: # Initialize the MCP server
30: mcp = FastMCP(
31:     "Personal Finance Advisor",
32:     instructions=(
33:         "Deterministic personal finance toolkit grounded in core financial-planning "
34:         "principles. Covers Time Value of Money, cash-flow & budgeting, debt "
35:         "management, Indian small-savings (PPF/SSY/NSC/KVP/SCSS/RD/FD/EPF), goal & "
36:         "retirement planning, stock/bond valuation, derivatives, mutual funds, portfolio "
37:         "analytics, risk profiling, and live market data (mutual-fund NAVs, FX, quotes).\n\n"
38:         "HOW TO ROUTE A USER STORY TO TOOLS:\n"
39:         "- The user will NOT name tools. Infer intent from their situation and pick tools "
40:         "by what they're trying to achieve.\n"
41:         "- When someone describes their finances broadly ('I'm 30, earn 1L/month, have a "
42:         "home loan, want to retire at 60'), START with `create_financial_plan` to get a "
43:         "prioritised action plan, then drill into specific calculators for detail.\n"
44:         "- Follow the planning order: evaluate position -> protect (emergency fund, "
45:         "insurance) -> reduce debt -> profile risk -> invest for goals.\n"
46:         "- Chain tools freely: e.g. assess_risk_profile -> suggest_asset_allocation -> "
47:         "calculate_sip_needed. Always show the numbers and the formula used.\n\n"
48:         "GOVERNANCE — STRICTLY FOLLOW (non-negotiable):\n"
49:         "1. Use ONLY numbers returned by these tools. Never invent, estimate, round "
50:         "differently, or substitute your own figures for a tool's output.\n"
51:         "2. Present allocations, percentages, EMIs, corpus and SIP amounts EXACTLY as "
52:         "the tool returned them. If you show a split, it must match the tool verbatim.\n"
53:         "3. Do NOT fabricate things the tools do not return: specific fund names or "
54:         "tickers, expected-return ranges, CAGR assumptions, tax rates, or multi-year "
55:         "projection tables. If the user wants a projection, call the relevant tool "
56:         "(e.g. plan_retirement, calculate_sip_returns) and report ITS numbers.\n"
57:         "4. There is ONE source of truth for an equity/debt/gold split: "
58:         "suggest_asset_allocation. assess_risk_profile returns the same split. If you "
59:         "have both, they will agree — never blend them or present a third number.\n"
60:         "5. If two tool results appear to conflict, do not silently pick one. Re-run "
61:         "with consistent inputs and surface the discrepancy to the user.\n"
62:         "6. Recompute via a tool whenever inputs change; never carry an earlier answer "
63:         "forward as if it still applies. State which tool produced each number."
64:     ),
65:     # Public HTTP connector: allow any host/origin (e.g. the Hugging Face Space
66:     # domain) and run stateless so it works behind a proxy / multiple workers.
67:     stateless_http=True,
68:     transport_security=TransportSecuritySettings(
69:         enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False,
70:         allowed_hosts=["*"],
71:         allowed_origins=["*"],
72:     ),
73: )
74: 
75: # Register all tool modules
76: 
77: tvm.register(mcp)
78: debt.register(mcp)
79: planning.register(mcp)
80: bonds.register(mcp)
81: stocks.register(mcp)
82: mutual_funds.register(mcp)
83: portfolio.register(mcp)
84: derivatives.register(mcp)
85: india_savings.register(mcp)
86: cashflow.register(mcp)
87: risk_profile.register(mcp)
88: advisor.register(mcp)
89: marketdata.register(mcp)
90: 
91: 
92: def main():
93:     """Run the MCP server with stdio transport."""
94:     mcp.run(transport="stdio")
95: 
96: 
97: if __name__ == "__main__":
98:     main()

1: """Output formatting utilities for MCP tool responses."""
2: 
3: 
4: def format_currency(amount: float, symbol: str = "₹") -> str:
5:     """Format number as Indian currency."""
6:     if amount < 0:
7:         return f"-{symbol}{abs(amount):,.2f}"
8:     return f"{symbol}{amount:,.2f}"
9: 
10: 
11: def format_percentage(value: float) -> str:
12:     """Format as percentage."""
13:     return f"{value:.2f}%"
14: 
15: 
16: def format_section(title: str, content: dict, indent: int = 2) -> str:
17:     """Format a section with title and key-value pairs."""
18:     lines = [f"\n{'═' * 50}", f"  {title}", f"{'═' * 50}"]
19:     prefix = " " * indent
20: 
21:     for key, value in content.items():
22:         if key in ("formula", "reference"):
23:             continue
24:         display_key = key.replace("_", " ").title()
25:         if isinstance(value, float):
26:             if (
27:                 "ratio" in key
28:                 or "rate" in key
29:                 or "pct" in key
30:                 or "yield" in key
31:                 or "return" in key
32:             ):
33:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}{display_key}: {format_percentage(value)}")
34:             elif abs(value) >= 100:
35:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}{display_key}: {format_currency(value)}")
36:             else:
37:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}{display_key}: {value}")
38:         elif isinstance(value, dict):
39:             lines.append(f"{prefix}{display_key}:")
40:             for k, v in value.items():
41:                 k_display = k.replace("_", " ").title()
42:                 if isinstance(v, float) and abs(v) >= 100:
43:                     lines.append(f"{prefix}  {k_display}: {format_currency(v)}")
44:                 else:
45:                     lines.append(f"{prefix}  {k_display}: {v}")
46:         elif isinstance(value, list) and value and isinstance(value[0], dict):
47:             lines.append(f"{prefix}{display_key}:")
48:             for item in value[:10]:  # limit list output
49:                 item_str = " | ".join(
50:                     f"{k}: {format_currency(v) if isinstance(v, float) and abs(v) >= 100 else v}"
51:                     for k, v in item.items()
52:                 )
53:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}  {item_str}")
54:             if len(value) > 10:
55:                 lines.append(f"{prefix}  ... and {len(value) - 10} more rows")
56:         else:
57:             lines.append(f"{prefix}{display_key}: {value}")
58: 
59:     return "\n".join(lines)
60: 
61: 
62: def format_tool_response(title: str, result: dict, reference: str = "") -> str:
63:     """Format complete tool response with title, results, formula, and reference."""
64:     output = format_section(title, result)
65: 
66:     if "formula" in result:
67:         output += f"\n\n  Formula: {result['formula']}"
68: 
69:     if reference:
70:         output += f"\n\n  Reference: {reference}"
71: 
72:     return output
73: 
74: 
75: def format_table(headers: list[str], rows: list[list], title: str = "") -> str:
76:     """Format data as ASCII table."""
77:     col_widths = [len(h) for h in headers]
78:     for row in rows:
79:         for i, cell in enumerate(row):
80:             col_widths[i] = max(col_widths[i], len(str(cell)))
81: 
82:     separator = "+" + "+".join("-" * (w + 2) for w in col_widths) + "+"
83:     header_line = (
84:         "|" + "|".join(f" {h:<{col_widths[i]}} " for i, h in enumerate(headers)) + "|"
85:     )
86: 
87:     lines = []
88:     if title:
89:         lines.append(f"\n  {title}")
90:     lines.append(separator)
91:     lines.append(header_line)
92:     lines.append(separator)
93:     for row in rows:
94:         row_line = (
95:             "|"
96:             + "|".join(f" {str(cell):<{col_widths[i]}} " for i, cell in enumerate(row))
97:             + "|"
98:         )
99:         lines.append(row_line)
100:     lines.append(separator)
101: 
102:     return "\n".join(lines)

1: """
2: Bond Pricing and Yield Calculations
3: 
4: Core formulas:
5:   Bond Price = Σ [C/(1+r)^t] + FV/(1+r)^n
6:   Current Yield = Annual Coupon / Market Price
7:   YTM: Price = Σ [C/(1+y)^t] + FV/(1+y)^n  (solved iteratively)
8:   Macaulay Duration = Σ [t × PV(CF_t)] / Bond Price
9:   Modified Duration = Macaulay Duration / (1 + y/n)
10:   Convexity = Σ [t(t+1) × PV(CF_t)] / (Price × (1+y)^2)
11: """
12: 
13: 
14: def bond_price(
15:     face_value: float,
16:     coupon_rate: float,
17:     ytm: float,
18:     years_to_maturity: float,
19:     coupon_frequency: int = 2,
20: ) -> dict:
21:     """
22:     Calculate bond price using DCF.
23:     Price = Σ [C/(1+r)^t] + FV/(1+r)^n
24:     """
25:     c = face_value * (coupon_rate / 100) / coupon_frequency
26:     r = ytm / 100 / coupon_frequency
27:     n = int(years_to_maturity * coupon_frequency)
28: 
29:     if r == 0:
30:         pv_coupons = c * n
31:         pv_face = face_value
32:     else:
33:         pv_coupons = c * (1 - (1 + r) ** (-n)) / r
34:         pv_face = face_value / (1 + r) ** n
35: 
36:     price = pv_coupons + pv_face
37: 
38:     if price > face_value:
39:         premium_discount = "Premium (Price > Face Value)"
40:     elif price < face_value:
41:         premium_discount = "Discount (Price < Face Value)"
42:     else:
43:         premium_discount = "At Par"
44: 
45:     return {
46:         "bond_price": round(price, 2),
47:         "pv_of_coupons": round(pv_coupons, 2),
48:         "pv_of_face_value": round(pv_face, 2),
49:         "coupon_per_period": round(c, 2),
50:         "total_periods": n,
51:         "premium_or_discount": premium_discount,
52:         "premium_discount_amount": round(price - face_value, 2),
53:         "formula": f"Price = Σ[{c:.2f}/(1+{r:.4f})^t] + {face_value}/(1+{r:.4f})^{n}",
54:     }
55: 
56: 
57: def current_yield(annual_coupon: float, market_price: float) -> dict:
58:     """Current Yield = Annual Coupon / Market Price"""
59:     cy = (annual_coupon / market_price) * 100
60: 
61:     return {
62:         "current_yield": round(cy, 4),
63:         "annual_coupon": annual_coupon,
64:         "market_price": market_price,
65:         "formula": f"CY = {annual_coupon} / {market_price} × 100 = {cy:.4f}%",
66:     }
67: 
68: 
69: def yield_to_maturity(
70:     face_value: float,
71:     coupon_rate: float,
72:     market_price: float,
73:     years_to_maturity: float,
74:     coupon_frequency: int = 2,
75: ) -> dict:
76:     """
77:     Calculate YTM using iterative Newton-Raphson method.
78:     Solve: Price = Σ [C/(1+y)^t] + FV/(1+y)^n for y
79:     """
80:     c = face_value * (coupon_rate / 100) / coupon_frequency
81:     n = int(years_to_maturity * coupon_frequency)
82: 
83:     # Approximate YTM using formula:
84:     # YTM ≈ [C + (FV - P)/n] / [(FV + P)/2]
85:     annual_coupon = face_value * coupon_rate / 100
86:     approx_ytm = (annual_coupon + (face_value - market_price) / years_to_maturity) / (
87:         (face_value + market_price) / 2
88:     )
89: 
90:     # Newton-Raphson refinement
91:     ytm_guess = approx_ytm / coupon_frequency
92: 
93:     for _ in range(200):
94:         price = 0
95:         dprice = 0
96:         for t in range(1, n + 1):
97:             df = (1 + ytm_guess) ** t
98:             price += c / df
99:             dprice -= t * c / (df * (1 + ytm_guess))
100:         price += face_value / (1 + ytm_guess) ** n
101:         dprice -= n * face_value / ((1 + ytm_guess) ** n * (1 + ytm_guess))
102: 
103:         diff = price - market_price
104:         if abs(diff) < 0.0001:
105:             break
106:         ytm_guess -= diff / dprice
107: 
108:     ytm_annual = ytm_guess * coupon_frequency * 100
109: 
110:     return {
111:         "ytm": round(ytm_annual, 4),
112:         "ytm_per_period": round(ytm_guess * 100, 4),
113:         "approximate_ytm": round(approx_ytm * 100, 4),
114:         "market_price": market_price,
115:         "face_value": face_value,
116:         "coupon_rate": coupon_rate,
117:         "formula": "YTM ≈ [C + (FV - P)/n] / [(FV + P)/2]",
118:     }
119: 
120: 
121: def bond_duration(
122:     face_value: float,
123:     coupon_rate: float,
124:     ytm: float,
125:     years_to_maturity: float,
126:     coupon_frequency: int = 2,
127: ) -> dict:
128:     """
129:     Calculate Macaulay Duration and Modified Duration.
130:     Macaulay: D = Σ [t × PV(CF_t)] / Price
131:     Modified: D_mod = D_mac / (1 + y/n)
132:     """
133:     c = face_value * (coupon_rate / 100) / coupon_frequency
134:     r = ytm / 100 / coupon_frequency
135:     n = int(years_to_maturity * coupon_frequency)
136: 
137:     price = 0
138:     weighted_pv = 0
139: 
140:     for t in range(1, n + 1):
141:         cf = c if t < n else c + face_value
142:         pv = cf / (1 + r) ** t
143:         price += pv
144:         weighted_pv += t * pv
145: 
146:     macaulay_duration = weighted_pv / price  # in periods
147:     macaulay_years = macaulay_duration / coupon_frequency
148:     modified_duration = macaulay_years / (1 + r)
149: 
150:     # Price sensitivity
151:     price_change_1pct = -modified_duration * 1  # % change for 1% rate increase
152: 
153:     return {
154:         "macaulay_duration_periods": round(macaulay_duration, 4),
155:         "macaulay_duration_years": round(macaulay_years, 4),
156:         "modified_duration": round(modified_duration, 4),
157:         "bond_price": round(price, 2),
158:         "price_change_for_1pct_rate_rise": round(price_change_1pct, 4),
159:         "interpretation": f"For every 1% increase in yield, bond price drops approximately {abs(price_change_1pct):.2f}%",
160:         "formula": "D_mac = Σ[t × PV(CF_t)] / Price; D_mod = D_mac / (1 + y/n)",
161:     }

1: """
2: Stock Valuation Models
3: 
4: Models:
5:   Gordon Growth (DDM): P = D1 / (r - g)
6:   Multi-stage DDM: P = Σ[D_t/(1+r)^t] + P_n/(1+r)^n
7:   P/E Valuation: Fair Price = EPS × Industry P/E
8:   DCF: P = Σ[FCF_t/(1+WACC)^t] + TV/(1+WACC)^n
9:   PEG Ratio = P/E / Earnings Growth Rate
10: """
11: 
12: 
13: def gordon_growth_model(
14:     current_dividend: float, growth_rate: float, required_return: float
15: ) -> dict:
16:     """
17:     Gordon Growth Model (Constant Growth DDM).
18:     P = D1 / (r - g) where D1 = D0 × (1 + g)
19:     """
20:     g = growth_rate / 100
21:     r = required_return / 100
22: 
23:     if r <= g:
24:         return {"error": "Required return must be greater than growth rate"}
25: 
26:     d1 = current_dividend * (1 + g)
27:     price = d1 / (r - g)
28:     dividend_yield = d1 / price * 100
29: 
30:     return {
31:         "intrinsic_value": round(price, 2),
32:         "next_year_dividend": round(d1, 2),
33:         "dividend_yield": round(dividend_yield, 2),
34:         "growth_rate": growth_rate,
35:         "required_return": required_return,
36:         "formula": f"P = D1 / (r - g) = {d1:.2f} / ({r} - {g})",
37:     }
38: 
39: 
40: def multi_stage_ddm(
41:     current_dividend: float,
42:     high_growth_rate: float,
43:     high_growth_years: int,
44:     stable_growth_rate: float,
45:     required_return: float,
46: ) -> dict:
47:     """
48:     Two-stage Dividend Discount Model.
49:     Stage 1: High growth period with DDM
50:     Stage 2: Stable growth with Gordon model
51:     """
52:     r = required_return / 100
53:     g1 = high_growth_rate / 100
54:     g2 = stable_growth_rate / 100
55: 
56:     if r <= g2:
57:         return {"error": "Required return must exceed stable growth rate"}
58: 
59:     # Stage 1: PV of dividends during high growth
60:     pv_stage1 = 0
61:     dividend = current_dividend
62:     dividends = []
63: 
64:     for t in range(1, high_growth_years + 1):
65:         dividend = dividend * (1 + g1)
66:         pv = dividend / (1 + r) ** t
67:         pv_stage1 += pv

name: analyzing-repositories
description: Analyzes repository structures, detects programming languages, frameworks, package managers, and existing test inventory. Use when assessing a new codebase or preparing for test generation.

---

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step
The platform runs the scan in code, not as a skill script. Given the repository directory, it returns JSON (languages, frameworks, test runners, manifests, source/test file counts, detected `mode`) and writes nothing. Implemented in `repos/scan.py`.

## Edge Cases
- **Monorepos:** Detect workspace roots (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, lerna, cargo workspaces) and shard analysis per package.
- **Minified Files:** Flag minified bundles and request unminified source code.

# Extracting Requirements

Reverse-engineers observable functional behavior into structured, traceable requirements without hallucination.

## When to use
Activate when the requirements stage runs (plugin command `qe-requirements`), or whenever deriving testable behavior from source code, API routes, or Jira stories.

## Workflow
0. **Mode:** Brownfield reads code. Greenfield reads the approved user stories file (`docs/qe/<app>/02-requirements/user_stories.md`) instead of code.
1. **Source Inspection:** Locate route handlers, controllers, CLI command parsers, and business rules.
2. **Behavior Identification:** Express requirements in observable terms ("System returns 403 when token is expired").
3. **Evidence Extraction:** Brownfield: copy exact verbatim source quotes with `file:line` citations. Greenfield: quote the story ID plus the acceptance criterion text verbatim (e.g. `US-CALC-002 AC2: "Then an error 'Cannot divide by zero' is shown"`).
4. **Actor Classification:** Assign every requirement to an actor (`anonymous`, `customer`, `admin`, `system`).
5. **Output Delivery:** Produce `02-requirements/requirements.json` and present for Gate 1 human approval.

## Strict Rules
- See [references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md](references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md) for anti-hallucination and evidence guidelines.

## Platform code step
Before Gate 1 is presented, the platform runs the contract check in code (planned: `qe/contracts.py`, not yet built). It returns `{accepted, rejected}` and fails if any requirement has no evidence quote or, when a repository root is given (brownfield), if the quote is not found verbatim in its source file. Drop or fix every rejected requirement. It writes nothing.

1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |
55: |----------|:----:|----------|
56: | Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
57: | Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
58: | Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
59: | Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
60: | Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
61: | Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
62: | Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
63: | Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
64: | Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
65: | Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
66: | Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
67: | Risk Profiling | 1 | suitability score → suggested equity/debt split |
68: | Advisor | 1 | `create_financial_plan` — the story → plan orchestrator |
69: 
70: Browse them all (with live descriptions) at [`/tools`](https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/tools).
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## Quick start
75: 
76: ### Use the hosted connector (no install)
77: 
78: **Claude Desktop** — Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste:
79: 
80: ```
81: https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
82: ```
83: 
84: **Claude Code**
85: 
86: ```bash
87: claude mcp add --transport http personal-finance https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
88: ```
89: 
90: **Cursor / VS Code** — add to `mcp.json`:
91: 
92: ```json
93: {
94:   "mcpServers": {
95:     "personal-finance": {
96:       "url": "https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp",
97:       "transport": "http"
98:     }
99:   }
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: ### Install from PyPI (stdio server)
104: 
105: ```bash
106: pip install personal-finance-mcp     # or: uvx personal-finance-mcp
107: ```
108: 
109: Then point Claude Desktop at it:
110: 
111: ```json
112: {
113:   "mcpServers": {
114:     "personal-finance": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["personal-finance-mcp"] }
115:   }
116: }
117: ```
118: 
119: ### Run locally from source
120: 
121: ```bash
122: git clone https://github.com/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp.git
123: cd personal-finance-mcp
124: pip install -e .
125: 
126: # Option A — classic stdio MCP server (offline, no web)
127: python -m src
128: 
129: # Option B — unified server: website + /mcp connector + /api  (http://localhost:7860)
130: cd web && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
131: python -m src.web
132: ```
133: 
134: For stdio, point Claude Desktop at the local process:
135: 
136: ```json
137: {
138:   "mcpServers": {
139:     "personal-finance": { "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "src"] }
140:   }
141: }
142: ```

# Requirements Reverse-Engineering Rules

1. **Observable Behavior Rule:** Requirements must assert externally observable behavior (HTTP response codes, return values, emitted events, DOM changes). Never assert internal private variable state.
2. **Mandatory Source Quote Rule:** Every requirement must include:
   - `source_file`: relative path to real file.
   - `line_number`: 1-based start line.
   - `quote`: verbatim code snippet copied directly from source.
3. **Precedence Rule:** Executable code strictly takes precedence over comments. If a comment says "Always returns true" but code has an `if (...) return false;` branch, extract the real code behavior.
4. **Actors Rule:** Every requirement names exactly one actor or `system`.

1: """
2: Time Value of Money Calculations
3: 
4: Core formulas:
5:   FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Future Value with compounding
6:   PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Present Value
7:   FV_continuous = PV × e^(r×t)         -- Continuous compounding
8:   FV_annuity = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1)/r]  -- Future Value of Annuity
9:   PV_annuity = PMT × [(1 - (1+r)^-n)/r] -- Present Value of Annuity
10:   PV_perpetuity = PMT / r             -- Present Value of Perpetuity
11:   PV_growing_perpetuity = PMT / (r-g) -- Growing Perpetuity
12:   Rule of 72: Years to double ≈ 72 / rate
13: """
14: 
15: import math
16: 
17: 
18: def future_value(
19:     pv: float, annual_rate: float, years: float, compounding_periods: int = 1
20: ) -> dict:
21:     """Calculate Future Value with compounding. FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)"""
22:     r = annual_rate / 100
23:     n = compounding_periods
24:     t = years
25: 
26:     if n == 0:  # continuous compounding
27:         fv = pv * math.exp(r * t)
28:         formula = f"FV = PV × e^(r×t) = {pv:,.2f} × e^({r}×{t})"
29:     else:
30:         fv = pv * (1 + r / n) ** (n * t)
31:         formula = f"FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t) = {pv:,.2f} × (1 + {r}/{n})^({n}×{t})"
32: 
33:     simple_interest = pv * r * t
34:     compound_benefit = fv - pv - simple_interest
35: 
36:     return {
37:         "future_value": round(fv, 2),
38:         "present_value": pv,
39:         "total_interest": round(fv - pv, 2),
40:         "simple_interest": round(simple_interest, 2),
41:         "compounding_benefit": round(compound_benefit, 2),
42:         "growth_multiple": round(fv / pv, 4),
43:         "formula": formula,
44:     }
45:

47: def present_value(
48:     fv: float, annual_rate: float, years: float, compounding_periods: int = 1
49: ) -> dict:
50:     """Calculate Present Value. PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t)"""
51:     r = annual_rate / 100
52:     n = compounding_periods
53:     t = years
54: 
55:     if n == 0:  # continuous
56:         pv = fv * math.exp(-r * t)
57:         formula = f"PV = FV × e^(-r×t) = {fv:,.2f} × e^(-{r}×{t})"
58:     else:
59:         pv = fv / (1 + r / n) ** (n * t)
60:         formula = f"PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t) = {fv:,.2f} / (1 + {r}/{n})^({n}×{t})"
61: 
62:     discount = fv - pv
63: 
64:     return {
65:         "present_value": round(pv, 2),
66:         "future_value": fv,
67:         "discount": round(discount, 2),
68:         "discount_factor": round(pv / fv, 6),
69:         "formula": formula,
70:     }
71: 
72: 
73: def future_value_annuity(
74:     pmt: float,
75:     annual_rate: float,
76:     years: float,
77:     compounding_periods: int = 12,
78:     annuity_type: str = "ordinary",
79: ) -> dict:
80:     """
81:     Future Value of Annuity.
82:     Ordinary: FV = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1) / r]
83:     Due:      FV = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1) / r] × (1+r)
84:     """
85:     r = annual_rate / 100 / compounding_periods
86:     n = int(years * compounding_periods)
87:     total_invested = pmt * n
88: 
89:     if r == 0:
90:         fv = pmt * n
91:     else:
92:         fv = pmt * (((1 + r) ** n - 1) / r)
93:         if annuity_type == "due":
94:             fv *= 1 + r
95: 
96:     wealth_gained = fv - total_invested
97: 
98:     return {
99:         "future_value": round(fv, 2),
100:         "total_invested": round(total_invested, 2),
101:         "wealth_gained": round(wealth_gained, 2),
102:         "total_payments": n,
103:         "payment_amount": pmt,
104:         "effective_annual_rate": round((1 + r) ** compounding_periods - 1, 6) * 100,
105:         "formula": f"FV = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1) / r] = {pmt:,.2f} × [((1+{r:.6f})^{n} - 1) / {r:.6f}]",
106:     }
107:

111:     annual_rate: float,
112:     years: float,
113:     compounding_periods: int = 12,
114:     annuity_type: str = "ordinary",
115: ) -> dict:
116:     """
117:     Present Value of Annuity.
118:     Ordinary: PV = PMT × [(1 - (1+r)^-n) / r]
119:     Due:      PV = PMT × [(1 - (1+r)^-n) / r] × (1+r)
120:     """
121:     r = annual_rate / 100 / compounding_periods
122:     n = int(years * compounding_periods)
123: 
124:     if r == 0:
125:         pv = pmt * n
126:     else:
127:         pv = pmt * ((1 - (1 + r) ** (-n)) / r)
128:         if annuity_type == "due":

132:

136:         "total_interest": round(total_payments - pv, 2),
137:         "num_payments": n,
138:         "formula": f"PV = PMT × [(1 - (1+r)^-n) / r] = {pmt:,.2f} × [(1 - (1+{r:.6f})^-{n}) / {r:.6f}]",

143:     """
144:     Present Value of Perpetuity.
145:     Simple:  PV = PMT / r
146:     Growing: PV = PMT / (r - g)  where r > g
147:     """
148:     r = annual_rate / 100

150: 
151:     if growth_rate > 0:
152:         if r <= g:
153:             return {
154:                 "error": "Required return must be greater than growth rate for growing perpetuity"
155:             }
156:         pv = pmt / (r - g)
157:         formula = f"PV = PMT / (r - g) = {pmt:,.2f} / ({r} - {g})"

159:     else:

167:         "perpetuity_type": perpetuity_type,
168:         "formula": formula,

---
name: analyzing-repositories
description: Analyzes repository structures, detects programming languages, frameworks, package managers, and existing test inventory. Use when assessing a new codebase or preparing for test generation.
metadata:
  author: Sarvesh Talele
  version: "1.4.0"
---

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step
The platform runs the scan in code, not as a skill script. Given the repository directory, it returns JSON (languages, frameworks, test runners, manifests, source/test file counts, detected `mode`) and writes nothing. Implemented in `repos/scan.py`.

## Edge Cases
- **Monorepos:** Detect workspace roots (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, lerna, cargo workspaces) and shard analysis per package.
- **Minified Files:** Flag minified bundles and request unminified source code.

---
name: extracting-requirements
description: Inverts codebases, public interfaces, and documentation into observable, testable requirements with verifiable evidence quotes. Use when extracting test requirements or preparing for test planning.
metadata:
  author: Sarvesh Talele
  version: "1.4.0"
---

# Extracting Requirements

Reverse-engineers observable functional behavior into structured, traceable requirements without hallucination.

## When to use
Activate when the requirements stage runs (plugin command `qe-requirements`), or whenever deriving testable behavior from source code, API routes, or Jira stories.

## Workflow
0. **Mode:** Brownfield reads code. Greenfield reads the approved user stories file (`docs/qe/<app>/02-requirements/user_stories.md`) instead of code.
1. **Source Inspection:** Locate route handlers, controllers, CLI command parsers, and business rules.
2. **Behavior Identification:** Express requirements in observable terms ("System returns 403 when token is expired").
3. **Evidence Extraction:** Brownfield: copy exact verbatim source quotes with `file:line` citations. Greenfield: quote the story ID plus the acceptance criterion text verbatim (e.g. `US-CALC-002 AC2: "Then an error 'Cannot divide by zero' is shown"`).
4. **Actor Classification:** Assign every requirement to an actor (`anonymous`, `customer`, `admin`, `system`).
5. **Output Delivery:** Produce `02-requirements/requirements.json` and present for Gate 1 human approval.

## Strict Rules
- See [references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md](references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md) for anti-hallucination and evidence guidelines.

## Platform code step
Before Gate 1 is presented, the platform runs the contract check in code (planned: `qe/contracts.py`, not yet built). It returns `{accepted, rejected}` and fails if any requirement has no evidence quote or, when a repository root is given (brownfield), if the quote is not found verbatim in its source file. # Requirements Reverse-Engineering Rules

1. **Observable Behavior Rule:** Requirements must assert externally observable behavior (HTTP response codes, return values, emitted events, DOM changes). Never assert internal private variable state.
2. **Mandatory Source Quote Rule:** Every requirement must include:
   - `source_file`: relative path to real file.
   - `line_number`: 1-based start line.
   - `quote`: verbatim code snippet copied directly from source.
3. **Precedence Rule:** Executable code strictly takes precedence over comments. If a comment says "Always returns true" but code has an `if (...) return false;` branch, extract the real code behavior.
4. **Actors Rule:** Every requirement names exactly one actor or `system`.

1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |
55: |----------|:----:|----------|
56: | Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
57: | Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
58: | Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
59: | Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
60: | Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |

content:
1: """
2: Personal Finance MCP Server
3: 
4: A stateless MCP server providing deterministic personal finance calculations
5: for financial planning, investment analysis, and portfolio management.
6: 
7: Supports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and any MCP-compatible client.
8: Transport: stdio (default), SSE (optional).
9: """
10: 
11: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
12: from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings
13: from .tools import (
14:     tvm,
15:     debt,
16:     planning,
17:     bonds,
18:     stocks,
19:     mutual_funds,
20:     portfolio,
21:     derivatives,
22:     india_savings,
23:     cashflow,
24:     risk_profile,
25:     advisor,
26:     marketdata,
27: )
28: 
29: # Initialize the MCP server
30: mcp = FastMCP(
31:     "Personal Finance Advisor",
32:     instructions=(
33:         "Deterministic personal finance toolkit grounded in core financial-planning "
34:         "principles. Covers Time Value of Money, cash-flow & budgeting, debt "
35:         "management, Indian small-savings (PPF/SSY/NSC/KVP/SCSS/RD/FD/EPF), goal & "
36:         "retirement planning, stock/bond valuation, derivatives, mutual funds, portfolio "
37:         "analytics, risk profiling, and live market data (mutual-fund NAVs, FX, quotes).\n\n"
38:         "HOW TO ROUTE A USER STORY TO TOOLS:\n"
39:         "- The user will NOT name tools. Infer intent from their situation and pick tools "
40:         "by what they're trying to achieve.\n"
41:         "- When someone describes their finances broadly ('I'm 30, earn 1L/month, have a "
42:         "home loan, want to retire at 60'), START with `create_financial_plan` to get a "
43:         "prioritised action plan, then drill into specific calculators for detail.\n"
44:         "- Follow the planning order: evaluate position -> protect (emergency fund, "
45:         "insurance) -> reduce debt -> profile risk -> invest for goals.\n"
46:         "- Chain tools freely: e.g. assess_risk_profile -> suggest_asset_allocation -> "
47:         "calculate_sip_needed. Always show the numbers and the formula used.\n\n"
48:         "GOVERNANCE — STRICTLY FOLLOW (non-negotiable):\n"
49:         "1. Use ONLY numbers returned by these tools. Never invent, estimate, round "
50:         "differently, or substitute your own figures for a tool's output.\n"
51:         "2. Present allocations, percentages, EMIs, corpus and SIP amounts EXACTLY as "
52:         "the tool returned them. If you show a split, it must match the tool verbatim.\n"
53:         "3. Do NOT fabricate things the tools do not return: specific fund names or "
54:         "tickers, expected-return ranges, CAGR assumptions, tax rates, or multi-year "
55:         "projection tables. If the user wants a projection, call the relevant tool "
56:         "(e.g. plan_retirement, calculate_sip_returns) and report ITS numbers.\n"
57:         "4. There is ONE source of truth for an equity/debt/gold split: "
58:         "suggest_asset_allocation. assess_risk_profile returns the same split. If you "
59:         "have both, they will agree — never blend them or present a third number.\n"
60:         "5. If two tool results appear to conflict, do not silently pick one. Re-run "
61:         "with consistent inputs and surface the discrepancy to the user.\n"
62:         "6. Recompute via a tool whenever inputs change; never carry an earlier answer "
63:         "forward as if it still applies. State which tool produced each number."
64:     ),
65:     # Public HTTP connector: allow any host/origin (e.g. the Hugging Face Space
66:     # domain) and run stateless so it works behind a proxy / multiple workers.
67:     stateless_http=True,
68:     transport_security=TransportSecuritySettings(
69:         enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False,
70:         allowed_hosts=["*"],
71:         allowed_origins=["*"],
72:     ),
73: )
74: 
75: # Register all tool modules
76: 
77: tvm.register(mcp)
78: debt.register(mcp)
79: planning.register(mcp)
80: bonds.register(mcp)
81: stocks.register(mcp)
82: mutual_funds.register(mcp)
83: portfolio.register(mcp)
84: derivatives.register(mcp)
85: india_savings.register(mcp)
86: cashflow.register(mcp)
87: risk_profile.register(mcp)
88: advisor.register(mcp)
89: marketdata.register(mcp)
90: 
91: 
92: def main():
93:     """Run the MCP server with stdio transport."""
94:     mcp.run(transport="stdio")
95: 
96: 
97: if __name__ == "__main__":
98:     main()

1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |
55: |----------|:----:|----------|
56: | Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
57: | Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
58: | Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
59: | Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
60: | Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
61: | Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
62: | Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
63: | Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
64: | Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
65: | Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
66: | Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
67: | Risk Profiling | 1 | suitability score → suggested equity/debt split |
68: | Advisor | 1 | `create_financial_plan` — the story → plan orchestrator |
69: 
70: Browse them all (with live descriptions) at [`/tools`](https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/tools).
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## Quick start
75: 
76: ### Use the hosted connector (no install)
77: 
78: **Claude Desktop** — Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste:
79: 
80: ```
81: https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
82: ```
83: 
84: **Claude Code**
85: 
86: ```bash
87: claude mcp add --transport http personal-finance https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
88: ```
89: 
90: **Cursor / VS Code** — add to `mcp.json`:
91: 
92: ```json
93: {
94:   "mcpServers": {
95:     "personal-finance": {
96:       "url": "https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp",
97:       "transport": "http"
98:     }
99:   }
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: ### Install from PyPI (stdio server)
104: 
105: ```bash
106: pip install personal-finance-mcp     # or: uvx personal-finance-mcp
107: ```
108: 
109: Then point Claude Desktop at it:
110: 
111: ```json
112: {
113:   "mcpServers": {
114:     "personal-finance": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["personal-finance-mcp"] }
115:   }
116: }
117: ```
118: 
119: ### Run locally from source
120: 
121: ```bash
122: git clone https://github.com/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp.git
123: cd personal-finance-mcp
124: pip install -e .
125: 
126: # Option A — classic stdio MCP server (offline, no web)
127: python -m src
128: 
129: # Option B — unified server: website + /mcp connector + /api  (http://localhost:7860)
130: cd web && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
131: python -m src.web
132: ```
133: 
134: For stdio, point Claude Desktop at the local process:
135: 
136: ```json
137: {
138:   "mcpServers": {
139:     "personal-finance": { "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "src"] }
140:   }
141: }
142: ```
143:

name: extracting-requirements
description: Inverts codebases, public interfaces, and documentation into observable, testable requirements with verifiable evidence quotes. Use when extracting test requirements or preparing for test planning.
metadata:

---

# Extracting Requirements

Reverse-engineers observable functional behavior into structured, traceable requirements without hallucination.

## When to use
Activate when the requirements stage runs (plugin command `qe-requirements`), or whenever deriving testable behavior from source code, API routes, or Jira stories.

## Workflow
0. **Mode:** Brownfield reads code. Greenfield reads the approved user stories file (`docs/qe/<app>/02-requirements/user_stories.md`) instead of code.
1. **Source Inspection:** Locate route handlers, controllers, CLI command parsers, and business rules.
2. **Behavior Identification:** Express requirements in observable terms ("System returns 403 when token is expired").
3. **Evidence Extraction:** Brownfield: copy exact verbatim source quotes with `file:line` citations. Greenfield: quote the story ID plus the acceptance criterion text verbatim (e.g. `US-CALC-002 AC2: "Then an error 'Cannot divide by zero' is shown"`).
4. **Actor Classification:** Assign every requirement to an actor (`anonymous`, `customer`, `admin`, `system`).
5. **Output Delivery:** Produce `02-requirements/requirements.json` and present for Gate 1 human approval.

## Strict Rules
- See [references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md](references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md) for anti-hallucination and evidence guidelines.

## Platform code step
Before Gate 1 is presented, the platform runs the contract check in code (planned: `qe/contracts.py`, not yet built). It returns `{accepted, rejected}` and fails if any requirement has no evidence quote or, when a repository root is given (brownfield), if the quote is not found verbatim in its source file. Drop or fix every rejected requirement. It writes nothing.

name: planning-tests
description: Formulates risk-weighted test strategies, decomposing requirements across Unit, Integration, API, and UI/E2E levels without duplication. Use when organizing testing strategy.
metadata:
  author: Sarvesh Talele
  version: "1.4.0"
---

# Planning Tests

Architects the smallest, most complete test strategy for a target application, ranking test areas by risk.

## When to use
Activate when the plan stage runs (plugin command `qe-plan`), or when scoping and allocating test levels for approved requirements.

## Workflow
1. **Requirement Risk Scoring:** Score business impact, change volatility, and technical risk (P0, P1, P2).
2. **Level Allocation:** Assign each scenario to the lowest proving level according to [references/LEVEL_GUIDELINES.md](references/LEVEL_GUIDELINES.md).
3. **Three Levels Required:** Every plan allocates **Unit** (pure functions/classes, no I/O), **Integration** (API/service/DB boundary, in-process or with a test client) and **E2E** (browser via Playwright) cases. Skip a level only with a written reason in the plan (e.g. "no UI").
4. **De-duplication Check:** Eliminate scenarios duplicated across unit, API, and E2E layers.
5. **Independent Confidence Scoring:** Calculate `controls_covered`, `level_fit`, and `scenarios_derivable`.
6. **Output Delivery:** Produce `03-plan/strategy.md` and `03-plan/plan.json`.

## Platform code step
The platform scores the plan in code (`qe/model.py`). Given `{"controlsCovered": 0-40, "levelFit": 0-30, "scenariosDerivable": 0-30}`, it returns `{score, verdict}`: `APPROVED` at 100, `REVISE` from 70, otherwise `REJECT`. It writes nothing. The Python verdict word is `REJECTED`; see `skills/README.md`.

---
name: designing-test-cases
description: Designs structured test cases across positive, negative, exception, and boundary value scenarios with deterministic oracles. Use when detailing test case specifications.
metadata:
  author: Sarvesh Talele
  version: "1.4.0"
---

# Designing Test Cases

Designs thorough, automatable test cases adhering to ISTQB techniques and deterministic oracle standards.

## When to use
Activate when the design stage runs (plugin command `qe-design`), or when authoring granular test specifications for approved plan areas.

## Scenario Multiplicity Requirement
For every requirement or user story, this skill MUST produce:
- **Positive:** Nominal happy path scenario proving intended functionality.
- **Negative (2-3):** Rejection paths, malformed inputs, unauthorized access attempts.
- **Exception (1):** Error handling under service failures or system exceptions.
- **Boundary Value:** Edge extremes (minimum, maximum, 0, just-above, just-below).

## Test levels
Allocate cases across **Unit** (pure logic, no I/O), **Integration** (API/service/DB boundary) and **E2E** (browser via Playwright), as the plan allows. Record each case's optional JSON field `level`: `Unit | Integration | E2E`. A level may be skipped only with a written reason in the plan (e.g. "no UI"). `level` is not a table column.

## Output columns
Every case table uses exactly these 11 columns, in order: `TC ID | User Story ID | Scenario | Type | Precondition | Test Data | Steps | Expected Result | Priority | Automation Candidate | Remarks`.
- **Type mapping:** `Positive`, `Negative`, `Exception`; boundary cases are `Negative (Boundary)`.
- **Priority:** P1-P3. **Automation Candidate:** `Yes (<tool>)` or `No`.
- **User Story ID:** the story or requirement ID the case verifies.

## Oracle Types
See [references/ORACLE_TYPES.md](references/ORACLE_TYPES.md) for details on `specified`, `derived`, `metamorphic`, and `golden` oracles.

## Confidence review (per case)
After designing, the `confidence-reviewer` agent scores every case against the real repository: the component it tests (file, line, symbol), then `source_proven`, `correct_target`, `expected_derivable` and `fixture_validity`, out of 100. Save the result to `docs/qe/<app>/04-design/confidence.json`. The platform then checks it in code (`qe/confidence.py`, planned, not yet built) with kind `design`. The check covers the arithmetic and the verdict rule, and that every cited `file:line` exists; a missing citation makes the case REJECT. Fix each REVISE or REJECT case and review it again. Anything left is shown to the user at the gate.

## Platform code step
The platform checks the designed cases (a JSON array) in code. It returns `{count, errors}` and fails when a case lacks `caseId`, `scenario`, `expectedResult` or an oracle kind; fix every error and rerun. It writes nothing. See `skills/README.md` and `docs/AGENT_SKILLS_AND_MAF_SPECIFICATION.md`.

name: generating-test-code
description: Synthesizes compilable, idiomatic test source code (Playwright TS, Vitest, PyTest, JUnit 5, NUnit/xUnit/MSTest) with 1:1 case traceability. Use when generating automated test suites.
metadata:

# Generating Test Code

Emits concrete test automation source files conforming to the native framework and idiom of the target repository.

## When to use
Activate when the generate stage runs (plugin command `qe-generate`), or when converting approved design specifications into executable test code.

## Strict Standards
1. **One Case Per File:** Exactly one test declaration per emitted test file.
2. **Canonical Comment:** First line must contain `// CASE_ID: <case-id>`.
3. **No Placeholders:** Zero `pass`, `TODO`, ellipsis (`...`), or `assert True`.
4. **Clean Imports:** Only import dependencies present in repository manifests. Maximum 10 imports.
5. **UI tests:** Playwright locators come from the real page. See the Playwright section of [references/LANGUAGE_RULES.md](references/LANGUAGE_RULES.md).
6. **UI evidence:** Copy `assets/playwright.config.ts` into the project. Wrap each case step in `test.step(...)` and attach a step screenshot (`<CASE_ID> step N`) after key assertions.
7. **Rules per Language:** See [references/LANGUAGE_RULES.md](references/LANGUAGE_RULES.md). Pinned tool versions: [references/VERSIONS.md](references/VERSIONS.md).

## Platform code step
The platform emits the test in code (planned: `qe/emit.py`, not yet built). Given `{"caseId","scenario","route","assertion"}`, it returns a validated Playwright test and fails on an invalid `caseId` or route. It writes nothing; save the output only after the user approves the file. The invalid-test-code check that already exists is `invalid_test_code` in `qe/execution.py`.

---
name: executing-tests
description: Dispatches test execution to local isolated runner adapters, capturing traces, standard streams, and JUnit XML reports. Use when executing automated tests.
metadata:
  author: Sarvesh Talele
  version: "1.4.0"
---

# Executing Tests

Executes test suites using runner adapters in project-local environments with structured log streaming and timeout enforcement.

## When to use
Activate when the execute stage runs (plugin command `qe-execute`), or whenever invoking test runners to capture verified pass/fail execution evidence.

## Runner Adapters
Consult [references/RUNNER_REGISTRY.md](references/RUNNER_REGISTRY.md) for the allowed commands and report paths across Playwright, Vitest, PyTest, Maven and Gradle. Pinned tool versions: [references/VERSIONS.md](references/VERSIONS.md).

## Playwright UI runs
Set `BASE_URL` in the environment. If the Playwright MCP server is connected (`mcp__playwright__browser_navigate`, `mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot`), use `browser_snapshot` to read the real accessibility tree when a locator fails; otherwise read the page source. MCP setup is opt-in and never auto-started.

In greenfield mode the first run of test-first suites records a RED baseline: failures are expected until the app exists and are reported as baseline, not as defects.

## Screenshot evidence (required)
Run every UI suite with screenshots on (`screenshot: "on"`, or `testInfo.attach` per step). After the run, the platform copies them out of the Playwright report in code: it reads `results/playwright.json` and writes them to `docs/qe/<app>/06-execution/evidence/e2e`. It writes `<caseId>-<step>.png` for each image attachment (base64 bodies and files), keeps only real PNG or JPEG data up to 5 MB, and refuses paths outside the project. `test-results/` is cleaned by the next run, so a screenshot that is not copied here is lost. The Gate 5 report embeds every image in `06-execution/evidence/`, and the dashboard flags any it does not show. This copy step is planned in `qe/execution.py` and is not yet built.

## MCP evidence
After the UI suite runs, write a plan `[{caseId, url, title?}]` from each E2E case's page to `docs/qe/<app>/06-execution/evidence/mcp-plan.json`. The platform then drives the Playwright MCP server in code, headless, and writes `<caseId>.png`, `<caseId>.snapshot.md` and `mcp-evidence.json` to `docs/qe/<app>/06-execution/evidence/mcp/`. With `BASE_URL` set, only its exact origin (host and port) is visited. Without it, only `localhost` URLs on the ports named in the plan (or the configured port) are visited, and well-known service ports are refused. A page that redirects to any other origin is recorded as `ok: false`; the redirect is detected after the browser follows it. If the MCP server cannot start (offline, or required tooling missing), record "MCP evidence skipped: <reason>" and continue; test-runner screenshots remain the primary evidence. This step is planned and not yet built.

## Platform code steps
- **JUnit summary:** the platform parses the JUnit XML in code (`parse_junit` in `qe/execution.py`) and returns total, passed, failed, skipped, durationMs, status, failures and cases. It writes nothing.
- **Verdict:** given raw counts, the platform returns the verdict in code (`verdict` in `qe/execution.py`). It returns `INCONCLUSIVE` when total is 0.
- **Runs:** suites run through `run_suite` in `qe/execution.py`, in an isolated project-local environment with a timeout.

## Verdict Integrity Rule
A run is ONLY marked `PASS` if test evidence confirms at least one executed passing test and zero failures. Empty suites or configuration errors are strictly marked `INCONCLUSIVE`.

content:
1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |
55: |----------|:----:|----------|
56: | Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
57: | Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
58: | Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
59: | Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
60: | Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
61: | Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
62: | Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
63: | Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
64: | Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
65: | Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
66: | Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
67: | Risk Profiling | 1 | suitability score → suggested equity/debt split |
68: | Advisor | 1 | `create_financial_plan` — the story → plan orchestrator |
69: 
70: Browse them all (with live descriptions) at [`/tools`](https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/tools).
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## Quick start
75: 
76: ### Use the hosted connector (no install)
77: 
78: **Claude Desktop** — Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste:
79: 
80: ```
81: https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
82: ```
83: 
84: **Claude Code**
85: 
86: ```bash
87: claude mcp add --transport http personal-finance https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp
88: ```
89: 
90: **Cursor / VS Code** — add to `mcp.json`:
91: 
92: ```json
93: {
94:   "mcpServers": {
95:     "personal-finance": {
96:       "url": "https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp",
97:       "transport": "http"
98:     }
99:   }
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: ### Install from PyPI (stdio server)
104: 
105: ```bash
106: pip install personal-finance-mcp     # or: uvx personal-finance-mcp
107: ```
108: 
109: Then point Claude Desktop at it:
110: 
111: ```json
112: {
113:   "mcpServers": {
114:     "personal-finance": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["personal-finance-mcp"] }
115:   }
116: }
117: ```
118: 
119: ### Run locally from source
120: 
121: ```bash
122: git clone https://github.com/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp.git
123: cd personal-finance-mcp
124: pip install -e .
125: 
126: # Option A — classic stdio MCP server (offline, no web)
127: python -m src
128: 
129: # Option B — unified server: website + /mcp connector + /api  (http://localhost:7860)
130: cd web && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
131: python -m src.web
132: ```
133: 
134: For stdio, point Claude Desktop at the local process:
135: 
136: ```json
137: {
138:   "mcpServers": {
139:     "personal-finance": { "command": "python", "args": ["-m", "src"] }
140:   }
141: }
142: ```
143: 
144: ---
145:

147:

1: """
2: Cash Flow & Budgeting
3: 
4: Tools for household cash-flow analysis, savings rate, debt servicing capacity
5: and contingency (emergency) fund adequacy — the building blocks of evaluating
6: a client's financial position before any investing advice.
7: """
8: 
9: 
10: def cash_flow_statement(
11:     monthly_income: float,
12:     fixed_expenses: float,
13:     variable_expenses: float,
14:     emi: float = 0.0,
15: ) -> dict:
16:     """Monthly surplus, savings rate and expense ratio from a household cash flow."""
17:     total_outflow = fixed_expenses + variable_expenses + emi
18:     surplus = monthly_income - total_outflow
19:     savings_rate = (surplus / monthly_income * 100) if monthly_income else 0
20:     expense_ratio = (total_outflow / monthly_income * 100) if monthly_income else 0
21: 
22:     if savings_rate >= 30:
23:         verdict = "Excellent — strong surplus to invest"
24:     elif savings_rate >= 20:
25:         verdict = "Healthy savings rate"
26:     elif savings_rate >= 10:
27:         verdict = "Adequate, aim for 20%+"
28:     elif savings_rate >= 0:
29:         verdict = "Thin surplus — review variable spending"
30:     else:
31:         verdict = "Deficit — outflows exceed income"
32: 
33:     return {
34:         "monthly_income": monthly_income,
35:         "total_outflow": round(total_outflow, 2),
36:         "monthly_surplus": round(surplus, 2),
37:         "savings_rate": round(savings_rate, 2),
38:         "expense_ratio": round(expense_ratio, 2),
39:         "annual_surplus": round(surplus * 12, 2),
40:         "verdict": verdict,
41:         "formula": "Surplus = Income - (Fixed + Variable + EMI); Savings rate = Surplus / Income",
42:     }
43: 
44: 
45: def debt_to_income(monthly_emi_total: float, monthly_income: float) -> dict:
46:     """Debt-to-income (debt servicing) ratio and borrowing-capacity verdict."""
47:     dti = (monthly_emi_total / monthly_income * 100) if monthly_income else 0
48:     if dti <= 30:
49:         verdict = "Comfortable — room to borrow if needed"
50:     elif dti <= 40:
51:         verdict = "Acceptable upper limit (lenders' typical cap ~40%)"
52:     elif dti <= 50:
53:         verdict = "Stretched — avoid new debt"
54:     else:
55:         verdict = "Over-leveraged — prioritise debt reduction"
56:     return {
57:         "debt_to_income_ratio": round(dti, 2),
58:         "monthly_emi_total": monthly_emi_total,
59:         "monthly_income": monthly_income,
60:         "verdict": verdict,
61:         "max_prudent_emi": round(monthly_income * 0.40, 2),
62:         "additional_emi_capacity": round(
63:             max(monthly_income * 0.40 - monthly_emi_total, 0), 2
64:         ),
65:         "formula": "DTI = Total EMI / Monthly Income; prudent cap ≈ 40%",
66:     }
67: 
68: 
69: def contingency_fund(
70:     monthly_expenses: float,
71:     months_target: int = 6,
72:     existing_fund: float = 0.0,
73: ) -> dict:
74:     """Contingency / emergency fund target, gap and current coverage."""
75:     target = monthly_expenses * months_target
76:     gap = max(target - existing_fund, 0)
77:     months_covered = (existing_fund / monthly_expenses) if monthly_expenses else 0
78:     return {
79:         "target_fund": round(target, 2),
80:         "existing_fund": existing_fund,
81:         "shortfall": round(gap, 2),
82:         "months_currently_covered": round(months_covered, 1),
83:         "months_target": months_target,
84:         "status": "Funded" if gap == 0 else "Underfunded",
85:         "formula": "Target = Monthly Expenses × Months (3-6 typical, 12 if income volatile)",
86:     }
